intro: An example first-year budget for a brand-new program. Every college's numbers differ — these illustrate the shape: mostly people, very little capital.

example.label: Example Year 1 budget

lineItems.label: Head coach (1.0 FTE, both squads)
lineItems.note: One appointment covering a men's and a women's program

lineItems.label: Graduate assistants (2)
lineItems.note: One per program, or assistant stipends near $10,000 each

lineItems.label: Travel and competition
lineItems.note: Both squads — fall 15s and spring 7s, regional and drivable

lineItems.label: Team equipment (one-time)
lineItems.note: Posts, tackle bags, pads, medical — shared across both squads

lineItems.label: Playing kit
lineItems.note: About $100 per player on a five-year replacement cycle

lineItems.label: Training and off-field kit
lineItems.note: About $150 per player on a five-year replacement cycle

lineItems.label: Facilities
lineItems.note: Shares existing grass — no new build required

example.totalNote: Years 2–5 run at about $151,000 — the one-time equipment spend does not repeat.

highlights.label: Low capital
highlights.body: A rugby pitch fits existing grass, and posts are the only fixed capital item. No new field, no new building.

highlights.label: Enrollment-positive
highlights.body: Rugby carries one of the largest rosters in college sport at almost no per-athlete capital cost — a recruiting channel first, a team second.

highlights.label: Break-even is small
highlights.body: At typical net tuition, a program breaks even at roughly a dozen athletes in Year 1, while rosters grow from about 35 to 95 by Year 5.
